title: AI-assisted whole-pancreas MRI measurements correlate with CT attenuation
summary: In 158 paired MRI/CT examinations, whole-pancreas fat fraction and CT attenuation showed a Spearman correlation of −.755. A locally trained U-Net assisted part of the MRI annotation, with manual correction of every assisted segmentation. The retrospective study also found substantial slice-to-slice variability; it did not independently validate automated segmentation or disease prediction.
ai_technology: U-Net pancreas annotation assistance and CNN-based liver segmentation

source_review.scope: Original publication metadata, computational/annotation Methods, Results and bounded prior-work/limitations Discussion passages actually read.

evidence.tested: Of 543 potentially paired examinations, selection/exclusion yielded 158 subjects with MRI and non-contrast CT within six months, plus 59 MRI-only examinations for 217 total MRI measurements. Mean pancreatic MRI fat fraction correlated inversely with CT attenuation (Spearman −.755); slice-to-slice MRI variation increased with mean whole-pancreas fat fraction (Spearman .51). The prior CT-only study is acknowledged separately.
evidence.unknown: All pancreas masks were manually drawn or manually corrected after CNN assistance. The source does not quantify how many final subjects required learned assistance, and this is not a model-accuracy validation. The locally trained MRI U-Net requires independent testing according to the authors. Referral-based inclusion, exclusion of inflammatory/neoplastic disease, image-quality selection, imperfect MRI resolution and up-to-six-month modality separation constrain interpretation. No pancreatic histological ground truth or equivalence of fat measures is established by correlation, and demographics/diabetes associations are observational. The source extends earlier CT-only measurements; it is not a first discovery that fat and CT attenuation are related.
evidence.ai_role: A U-Net trained during the annotation process assisted later MRI masks before manual correction; a separate CNN estimated liver fat. Learned segmentation aided measurement collection, while conventional correlations provided the scientific result.
